To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nitrogen-borne organic compounds with excellent response for lead ions could be developed by introducing the functional groups of cyano and hydroxylamine into the carriers.

the nitrogen-bearing organic compounds, acting as carriers, could be divided into three categories according to their molecular structures: the first category includes bis-schiff base, which is the best carrier for lead ion selective electrode, the second category is pyridyl carboamide and the third category is acylhydroxlamine and phenylhydrazones.
the nitrogen-bonded organic compounds with different molecular structures are excellent carriers for lead (II) ions selective electrodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of new nitrogen-bearing organic compounds, and the application of the compounds as ion carriers in ionophore-based lead-ion selective electrodes.
the development of nitrogen-bearing organic compounds for lead-ion selective electrodes and provides an insight into the design of new carriers for other ion-selective electrodes.
the design, synthesis, and application of the nitrogen-containing organic compounds as sensing agents in lead (II) selective electrode.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nitrogen-containing organic compounds with the ability of forming stable complexes with Pb(II) are promising candidates for developing new lead ion-selective electrodes with good response characteristics.
nitrogen-containing organic compounds are the promising candidates to be the carrier of lead ion-selective electrodes.
the nitrogen-bonding organic compound, especially the nitrogen-bonded compound containing the cyano group, is a promising carrier for ionophore-doping membranes of the ion-selective electrodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nitrogen-bonded organic compounds are excellent sensing agents for lead ion-selective electrodes with excellent response.
the lead-ion selective electrode with the carrier containing a nitrogen-containing group and a carboxyl group in its molecule is more likely to have a better selectivity towards lead ion.
the nitrogen-containing organic compound with the ability of coordinating lead (II) ions and the presence of cyano groups would be the best candidate for the carrier of lead ion-selective electrode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carrier should contain nitrogen and oxygen atoms, and have the ability to form a stable complex with Pb2+ in order to achieve the best performance.

the nitrogen-bearing organic compounds with excellent response characteristics can be used to prepare lead ion-selective electrodes with high sensitivity, wide linear range, fast response and good selectivity, which is expected to be applied to environmental monitoring, food and agricultural product detection, clinical analysis, and so on.
the carrier is the key component for the ionophore-doping membrane, which determines the selectivity and sensitivity of the lead ion-selective electrode.
